title: Secrets Playbook: Rotations, Break-Glass, SIEM Export & Inventory Notes
content:
Purpose and scope:
This playbook describes operational procedures and pragmatic notes for secrets management at Redwood Inference: centralized vaulting, scheduled rotation, break-glass (emergency access) handling, credential inventory formatting, and exporting audit evidence for SIEM and compliance reviews.

Audience:
- Engineering oncall and infra ops
- Security engineers (incident response)
- Platform and SRE teams responsible for service identity and key lifecycle

High-level principles (short):
- Single source of truth: HashiCorp Vault is the canonical store for long-lived secrets. AWS Secrets Manager used for short-lived KMS-encrypted tokens where latency or regional failover requires it.
- Automated rotations by default; manual only for legacy exceptions with documented rationale.
- Break-glass keys are auditable, time-limited, and rotated after use.
- Audit log schema must be exported to SIEM nightly and available for ad-hoc evidence pulls.

Quick links (operational):
- Vault UI: https://vault.internal.redwood.ai
- Vault Ops runbook (read-only): Confluence SEC-Runbooks/Vault-Ops
- Rotation automation repo: https://github.com/redwood-inference/secret-rotation

Credential inventory (recommended CSV columns):
- credential_id, owner, service, type (api_key|ssh|tls|db|k8s-secret), vault_path, last_rotated (YYYY-MM-DD), rotation_freq_days, automated (yes/no), rbac_owner_group, environment (prod|staging|dev), external_uses (list), status (active|deprecated|archived), notes

Notes on population:
- Export from Vault using: vault list -format=json secret/metadata | jq . (ops-only). Sanitize before sharing.
- For AWS-managed secrets, use aws secretsmanager list-secrets --query and normalize fields to the CSV schema above.

Rotation policy (default):
- Service API keys (machine-to-machine): rotate every 90 days, automated pipeline kickoffs via rotation microservice.
- Database credentials issued by Vault's DB plugin: TTL 1h (dynamic), no manual rotation required.
- Long-lived SSH deploy keys: rotate every 180 days; move to short-lived session-based access where possible.
- TLS private keys: follow PKI owner guidance; rotate on expiry or risk event.

Automation architecture (notes):
- rotation-agent (K8s CronJob) triggers rotation flows. Pulls rotation plan from central rotation-schedule bucket (S3 encrypted).
- rotation-svc calls Vault Admin API: /v1/secret/rotate or specific plugin endpoints.
- On success: rotation-svc creates a rotation-event audit record in the audit-log stream and posts a summarized message to #infra-ops.

Sample rotation command (ops):
- Trigger a manual rotation for path secret/data/services/ingest-api:
  1) curl -s -X POST --header "X-Vault-Token: $VAULT_TOKEN" https://vault.internal.redwood.ai/v1/secret/rotate/services/ingest-api
  2) Verify: vault read secret/data/services/ingest-api | jq .data.metadata.last_rotated
  3) Confirm dependent services pulled the new credential (see deployment check below).

Deployment check (post-rotation):
- Confirm new secret was written to the expected path and version incremented.
- Tail app logs (k8s) for auth failures for 30m: kubectl -n prod logs -l app=ingest --since=30m | grep -i authentication
- If widespread auth failures, trigger rollback by re-instating previous secret version via vault kv metadata put -versions=... (ops escalation).

Break-glass procedure (emergency access):
1) Preconditions: Exec-level signoff recorded in PagerDuty incident. Break-glass only after incident triage concludes automated recovery not possible in target time window.
2) Break-glass token location: Encrypted S3 object (s3://redwood-breakglass), KMS-encrypted, accessible only by a short-lived IAM role (assume-role) with MFA enforced.
3) Access steps:
   - Assumerole into ops-breakglass role (sts assume-role) with step-up MFA.
   - Retrieve object: aws s3 cp s3://redwood-breakglass/ingest-emergency-key.enc - | gpg --decrypt
   - Use key only for the minimum action (restart job, flip feature flag, rotate service user).
4) Mandatory: Every use must be logged in the BreakGlass register (Confluence form link) within 30 minutes with: incident id, operator, justifying narrative, actions performed, artifacts (commands run, request ids).
5) Post-use actions: Rotate the broken-glass credential immediately and run a full access review for all principals who accessed the assume-role.

RBAC v2 integration (secrets-specific notes):
- Map vault paths to RBAC roles for least privilege. Example mapping:
  - secret/data/services/ingest-api -> role: svc-ingest-readwrite (allowed principals: svc-ingest-deployment, eng-platform-rotations)
  - secret/data/team/payments -> role: team-payments-admins
- Use groups from identity provider (IdP) as source of truth for RBAC v2 role members. Sync cadence: nightly.
- Automation principle: rotation-svc must be allowed Update and List on vault mount only for the rotation paths; do not grant delete privileges globally.

Audit log schema (recommended minimal fields for SIEM ingest):
- timestamp: ISO8601
- event_id: UUID
- actor: username or service principal
- actor_type: human|service
- action: read|create|update|delete|rotate|login|assume_role
- resource: vault_path or secret_id
- resource_type: secret|token|policy|role
- auth_method: vault-token|oidc|aws-iam
- outcome: success|failure
- request_id: trace id from request pipeline
- client_ip: optional
- vault_version: path version or plugin version

Mapping notes for SIEM export (Elastic SIEM example):
- Export pipeline should normalize event_id -> ecs.guid, timestamp -> @timestamp, actor -> user.name, resource -> file.path or event.dataset. Use a lightweight Logstash/Fluentd transform that drops PII from actor.email when exporting to PII-free collections.

Evidence automation (for audits):
- Nightly job assembles evidence bundle: credential-inventory.csv (current snapshot), last-90-days audit events for vault mounts, rotation pipeline run logs, and break-glass register CSV.
- Bundle stored in secure, immutable evidence bucket with object versioning and retention policy (90 days for standard audits, 365 days for SOC2 review). Hashes recorded in Confluence audit page for provenance.
- Manual pull: security-audit script (repo tools/audit) supports flags: --start --end --vault-paths. Example: python tools/audit --start 2025-01-01 --end 2025-01-31 --vault-paths secret/data/services/*

SIEM alerts to configure (examples):
- High priority: multiple failed auth attempts to central vault path within 10 minutes (possible credential compromise).
- Medium: rotation-svc reports failure for a critical path and no manual rotation attempt in 1 hour.
- Low: long-lived secret older than 180 days appears in inventory (stale key warning).

Incident playbook snippets (what to query quickly):
- Who accessed the secret? Query audit logs for resource==path and action in [read,update] ordered by timestamp.
- Which services could be impacted? Cross-reference inventory service column + k8s service account annotations.
- Has rotation been attempted? Check rotation-svc logs and rotation-events index in SIEM.

Common gotchas / informal notes (ops experience):
- Some legacy services still embed keys in container images. Track these in the inventory notes 'external_uses' column and schedule deprecation tickets.
- Vault UI token-based views can hide plugin-managed dynamic creds; always verify via API if in doubt.
- When rotating TLS certs, remember downstream caches (CDN, client trust stores) may retain old cert for TTL window.

Open action items (short):
- [ ] Add rotation health check endpoint to rotation-svc (Jonas)
- [ ] Add vault audit -> SIEM transform that redacts emails (Priya)
- [ ] Run a one-off inventory sweep for images containing API keys (Snyk + infra scan) (Samir)

Appendix: sample SIEM JSON event (single line example)
{"timestamp":"2025-02-03T21:12:09Z","event_id":"6b1f9b8c-2a77-4a7d-8f1e-3d45e9f0a9b2","actor":"svc-rotation","actor_type":"service","action":"rotate","resource":"secret/data/services/ingest-api","resource_type":"secret","auth_method":"vault-token","outcome":"success","request_id":"req-03f9a"}

If anything in this doc seems incomplete or you need the automation repos mapped to specific rotation targets, ping #infra-ops or add a comment on Confluence SEC-Runbooks/Vault-Ops.
